The eight kinds are visually distinguishable; the drinking glass is a single table object and is not presented as glass material.
meaningful_development: In one connected, hand-free visual sequence, the same eight objects are shown one at a time leaving the loose group and appearing in their distinct display positions. Each transition preserves exactly one cup, plate, spoon, bowl, fork, knife, drinking glass, and napkin; the object currently shown is locally paired with its bare label, while movement and position remain nonverbal staging rather than scored language or spatial knowledge.
resolution_or_stopping_state: The loose-object area is empty and exactly one cup, plate, spoon, bowl, fork, knife, drinking glass, and napkin are simultaneously visible in the eight completed display positions. The event stops at this complete eight-kind distinction; no object is added, duplicated, removed, fused, or substituted, and no use, ownership, food, material, color, order, or table-setting convention is established.
